checkpoints.description: [1/2] Reject malformed received_at values at record construction

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed a bad timestamp is stored and imported, then one such record makes every time-filtered list fail with a misleading generic error.
impact_assessment.benefits: Inbox records always carry parseable timestamps, so time filtering cannot be broken by a single bad capture or snapshot.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: snapshots or records with invalid timestamps are now refused, so README and ADR must follow; dependency: stdlib datetime only; concurrency: none; state: validation occurs before any write.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Parse in __post_init__ with a Z-tolerant fromisoformat, raise CorruptInboxError, and add failing-first tests for construction and import.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Done: received_at validated at construction; bad snapshots refused; Z suffix accepted; 79 tests green
[2/2] Done: README timestamp rule and ADR-013
[2/2] Phase 4 passed: 5/5 gates green, 79 tests
Task 'postbox-time' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Ignore OS-level client disconnects when writing HTTP responses

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed a normal client disconnect before reading the response produces a full ConnectionAbortedError traceback while the capture itself succeeds.
impact_assessment.benefits: Clean operator console; no confusing stack traces for routine disconnects.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, the HTTP status is unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: per-thread write path only; state: capture is persisted before the response is written.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Catch OSError around wfile.write with a documented hygiene allowance, and use a mocked wfile failing-first test.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Done: response writes tolerate client disconnect; 80 tests green
[2/2] Done: README note and ADR-014; hygiene marker placement corrected
[2/2] Phase 4 passed: 5/5 gates green, 80 tests
Task 'postbox-disconnect' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Cover common OAuth/API credential names in header and query redaction

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed X-Access-Token, Api-Key, access_token and refresh_token are stored verbatim despite redaction being enabled, defeating ADR-005.
impact_assessment.benefits: Common webhook and OAuth credentials are no longer persisted in the inbox file.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: more fields are redacted, so README and ADR must follow; dependency: none; concurrency: pure functions, no state risk; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Extend the exact-match sets, add known-answer tests for each new name, and verify replay still skips redacted headers.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Report the OS-assigned port when serve uses --port 0

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed port 0 binds to a real port (64944) while the CLI advertises http://127.0.0.1:0, which nobody can connect to.
impact_assessment.benefits: The startup message is always a usable URL, including for ephemeral-port runs.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: only the startup message changes; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Derive the URL from server_address after binding, add a failing-first test on a real bound server, and keep the fixed-port message unchanged.
